text:
maya: Heads up, sample app showing generator-based streaming is flaky under client timeouts. If I set a short deadline on the parent ctx some stream goroutines never exit.

maya: Repro sketch:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 150*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()

stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }

var wg sync.WaitGroup
for chunk := range stream.Iterator() {
    wg.Add(1)
    go func(c Chunk) {
        defer wg.Done()
        processChunk(ctx, c)
    }(chunk)
}
// expect the iterator loop to end when ctx times out; wg.Wait() should finish quickly
wg.Wait()
```

maya: But with deadline=150ms the process sometimes hangs and `goroutine 88` shows an active `readLoop` inside the SDK that's stuck in a syscall.

zach: Two angles: (A) deadline vs cancel semantics. With timeout the ctx is cancelled by the runtime but socket-level reads might be blocked without a read deadline on the net.Conn, so the goroutine can't observe ctx.Done(). (B) your worker goroutines are using the same ctx for processing; if you keep passing the expired ctx to processChunk they'll block on anything that selects ctx.Done(). Consider deriving a child ctx with fallback for processing or early return.

leo: Also, using range over `stream.Iterator()` is fine but make sure Iterator() returns a channel that is closed when the internal reader exits. IIRC older generator iterator used an unbuffered channel and a single reader goroutine; that reader could be blocked on Read and not close the channel until connection breaks.

maya: Hmm, I did not set net transport deadlines. I'm on linux so I thought TCP read would unblock on context cancel but apparently not.

zach: Go's net.Conn doesn't honor context cancellation unless you use deadline-aware APIs. The SDK should call SetReadDeadline when you give a ctx with deadline. I don't think it currently does for short deadlines.

leo: Workarounds: 1) wrap the transport dialer with a custom net.Dialer and set ReadTimeouts, 2) avoid tight deadlines on parent ctx and instead cancel explicitely with cancel(), 3) call stream.Close() in a separate goroutine when ctx.Done() fires. Example: `go func(){ <-ctx.Done(); stream.Close() }()`

maya: I tried 'go func(){ <-ctx.Done(); stream.Close() }()' and it helped mostly, but CI still shows intermittent leftover goroutines in infra logs.

infra-bot: FYI a devbox reproducer traced by pstack shows blocked syscall: `read(4, 0x7ffd..., 4096)`.

leo: We should: a) make the SDK set a short read deadline (like 250ms) when ctx has a deadline so reads can be interrupted and the goroutine can select on ctx.Done(); b) make Stream.Close() idempotent and safe from other goroutines (if not already).

zach: I'll open a PR for the read-deadline behavior and add a feature flag so we can toggle it. Also will add integration tests that run with tight ctx timeouts to prevent regressions.

maya: For immediate sample app changes I'm going to: - stop using the same ctx for processing (derive a background child for computation), - add an explicit goroutine that closes the stream on ctx.Done(), and - add `defer stream.Close()` right after open.

maya: New sample patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/751. It documents the `ctx vs processing` pattern.

ci-bot: Ran the sample e2e on PR 751; leak frequency reduced but 1/10 runs still leaves 1 goroutine in `ioRead` state.

zach: After the read-deadline PR lands I'll re-run CI. Also suggest adding a snippet in docs showing the recommended pattern: `defer stream.Close(); go func(){ <-ctx.Done(); stream.Close() }(); for ... { go process(copyOfChunk) }` and note caveats for short deadlines.

leo: We should also provide a convenience helper `client.Generator.StreamWithCancel(ctx, req)` that returns a stream whose Close is automatically called when ctx.Done() triggers. Low-friction for users.

maya: Agreed. For now sample updates + the SDK read-deadline change should be enough. I'll watch the infra CI and report flakiness reduction. Thanks!
